items.definition:
To make something normal or standard.
We need to normalize the data before analysis.

To be more important or significant than.
The benefits of the new policy far outweigh the risks.

To stay just below the boiling point while being heated.
Let the sauce simmer gently for 20 minutes.

to make more efficient
We need to streamline our processes to reduce costs and save time.

to add a slight color to
She decided to tint her hair a lighter shade of brown.

to carry or haul
He had to tote the heavy bags of groceries all the way home.

to make a small adjustment
He needed to tweak the settings on his computer to improve performance.

to form a mental image of
Try to visualize your success before you begin the task.

to make someone believe something by repeatedly telling them that it is true
Some cults try to brainwash their members.

to cause (someone) to feel consternation and distress
The news of the cancellation dismayed the fans.

to purify (a liquid) by vaporizing it and then condensing it
They distill fresh water from the ocean.

engrave, carve
The artist will etch the design onto the glass.

admit (someone) to a position or organization
He was inducted into the Hall of Fame last year.

subdue (someone or something) by force; restrain
He tried to repress his anger.

inflict harm in return for an injury or wrong suffered
He vowed to avenge his brother's death.

think deeply about something that makes one unhappy
He continued to brood over his past mistakes.

make (a garment or piece of fabric) with yarn or thread and a hooked needle
My grandmother loves to crochet blankets for her grandchildren.

dig up
Archaeologists plan to excavate the ancient site next spring.

To poke with a finger, foot, or pointed object.
He had to prod his friend to get him to wake up.

To sink, droop, or hang especially in the middle.
The old shelf began to sag under the weight of the books.

to flow in a small stream
Water began to trickle from the leaky faucet.

to gather or accumulate a large amount
He began to amass a fortune.

to sell goods, typically by shouting in the street
Street vendors were hawking their wares.

Measure
It's difficult to quantify happiness.

Narrate
He began to recount the events of the day.

Experience again
She tried to relive her glory days.

to make sad
It would sadden me to see you leave.

to choke, to suffocate
He tried to strangle the attacker.

to hit or kick (the ball) before it touches the ground.
The player managed to volley the ball into the net.

to have an intense feeling of longing for something.
She yearned for her homeland.

to make or cause to make the slightest movement.
The heavy box wouldn't budge.

to come together from different directions
All roads converge at the city center.

to reduce to a lower rank or level
The company decided to downgrade the software to an older version.

to wet thoroughly; soak
The sudden rainstorm drenched us completely.

praise, worship
The song tends to glorify violence.

to make seem less important
His earlier achievements were overshadowed by his later failures.

to make a new master recording of (audio or video)
They decided to remaster the classic album.

to cut off the head of
In ancient times, traitors were often sentenced to be beheaded.

to arrange or set up
You need to configure the settings before using the software.

to struggle to deal with or overcome (a difficulty or problem)
He had to grapple with the difficult decision.

to carry out (a task) badly or carelessly
The mechanic really botched the repair job on my car.

to distort the shape or form of; to disfigure
High temperatures can deform plastic objects.

to take weapons away from; to remove hostility
The police officer managed to disarm the suspect without incident.

to defend oneself from a blow, attack, or attacker
She had to fend off several aggressive dogs during her walk.

extend the duration of
They tried to prolong their vacation for another week.

make (something) widely known
The company hired a firm to publicize their new product.

walk for pleasure, typically without a definite route; talk or write at length in a confused or inconsequential way
He tends to ramble when he's nervous.

direct (something) to a different place or purpose
The website will automatically redirect you to the new page.

demand or specify a requirement
The contract stipulates that payments must be made monthly.

to pacify or placate
He tried to appease his angry parents.

to consider one thing to be the same as or equivalent to another
You shouldn't equate wealth with happiness.

To twist or entangle together.
The branches of the two trees intertwined over the years.

capture again; experience again
The police managed to recapture the escaped prisoner.

drive or force back or away
The strong odor of garlic can repel mosquitoes.

to make things happen at the same time
We need to synchronize our watches.

shorten
We often abbreviate long words.

to act against something to reduce its effect
Exercise can help to counteract the effects of stress.

to make or become deeper
Their friendship began to deepen over time.

to put out (a fire or light)
The firefighters worked quickly to extinguish the blaze.

to stare with an open mouth; to open wide
The crowd stood gaping at the spectacular fireworks display.

suddenly spring or flinch back in fear, horror, or disgust
She recoiled in horror at the sight of the snake.

produce or be filled with a deep, full, reverberating sound; evoke or suggest images, memories, or emotions
His speech resonated with the audience, who shared his views.

to spread out in an untidy way
The city continued to sprawl outwards, consuming more farmland.

to dig up from the earth; to discover
Archaeologists hope to unearth ancient artifacts at the site.
